newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romanian bank changes board ahead restructuring.
newsitem.headline: Romanian bank changes board ahead restructuring.

text.p: Shareholders of Romania's state-run bank Banca Agricola SA (BA) this week appointed a new board, expected to unveil within a month a restructuring plan of the farm lender and pave the way for its selloff.
A bank statement said on Friday the State Ownership Fund (FPS) -- the majority holder of the BA -- along with the new board would analyse the bank's activity each month.

Banca Agricola has been the main channel for government aid to farmers. Its restructuring is one of several conditions Romania must meet under a World Bank Financial and Enterprise Structural Adjustment Loan (FESAL).

Last month, the World Bank unlocked a second tranche of $80 million from the $280 million FESAL, which it suspended in 1996 after criticising the slow pace of reforms under the leftist government ousted in last November's election.
The new centrist government issued a decree aimed at clarifying the BA's credit portfolio two weeks ago, authorising the bank to draw up a special balance sheet.

The decree said the difference between loans and interest considered losses and their collateral, totalling up to 2.7 trillion lei, will be settled with the help from the Finance Ministry, the FPS and the central bank.

It said the Finance Ministry would take on public debt up to 1.3 trillion lei and the central bank would reflect in a separate account the soft credits it gave BA until those loans are recouped from 1997-1999 financial results.

The FPS will give the bank 300 billion lei in aid by end-August and a further 200 billion by the end of 1997. It holds around 54 percent of BA's capital of 30.7 billion lei. The rest belongs to local investment funds, companies and individuals.
Banca Agricola is the third of Romania's six state-run banks due to be privatised under a bank selloff law.

The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development last year allowed its equity conversion rights on a $12 million technology loan to BA to lapse due to delays in the law. International lenders had insisted on passage and implementation of such legislation.
In April, Banca Agricola reported 147 billion lei net profit last year, when total assets were 8.2 trillion lei, or 41.5 percent up from 1995. ($=7,285 lei)
